correctness.rationale: In any finite commutative chain ring of length m with residue field q, each nonzero valuation shell has probability a*q^{-j} (a=1-1/q), zero has q^{-m}, and pairwise annihilation iff vi+vj>=m. For r=2, multiplying each shell by annihilator size q^j proves P(E)=q^{-m}(1+ma), asymptotically uniform first split and independent geometric overshoot G. For fixed r>=3 and m=2h+epsilon, centered feasible vector ui=vi-h satisfies ui+uj>=epsilon. Even epsilon=0 lattice cases are all ui>=0 or one negative -t and remaining >=t; odd epsilon=1 cases are all ui>=1 or one -t>=0 and others >=t+1. Geometric sums yield exactly both displayed Z_{r,q,epsilon}; their convergence is equivalent to r>2. A summable envelope a^{-r}q^{-sum ui} permits dominated convergence in l1, proving total variation, probability asymptotics and negligible zero/collision entries. Independent exact valuation-shell calculations verified the r=2 normalization for q=2,3 and m=2..11 and finite truncations of both lattice partition sums.
